title: CurvSegFlow: Time-Conditioned Flow Matching for Robust Segmentation of Curvilinear Structures in Noisy Biomedical Images
mechanism: Segmentation as time-conditioned flow matching: a U-Net with temporal embeddings integrates a learned velocity field from a noisy start to the mask, giving gradual error correction and better continuity at low SNR.
adaptation: Use as a refinement head: start the flow from house-model crack probabilities instead of noise, condition on 1-channel EL, few Euler steps; target the 7% of crack components that are < 2% darker than surroundings.
min_experiment: Arm: flow-matching refiner from house probabilities, 5 seeds. Baseline: house ensemble. Metrics: relF1@2, components found, crack IoU on 5-fold CV. Kill: relF1@2 < +0.005 after 2 days of tuning.
evidence: R: competitive or better than standard segmenters on synthetic and real microtubules, retinal vessels, corneal nerves, coronary arteries; largest gains in precision and continuity at low SNR (numbers not read).
prior_overlap: none; diffusion / flow segmenters never tried.
